clips.title: The story
paras: This trial, set directly by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, tasks rising heroes with hunting down the great kodo beast Arra'chea across the plains of Mulgore. Though an initiate may have completed the traditional rites of passage, Cairne expects his people to continually reaffirm their strength, tracking, and devotion to the tribe. Returning with Arra'chea's horn proves an adventurer is ready to serve the wider Horde beyond the mesas.

Reaching Thunder Bluff marks the end of simple youth for a tauren, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof does not let young hunters rest on their laurels. To Cairne, earning a place among the high bluffs is merely the beginning of one's responsibility to the United Tauren Tribes. Rather than sending initiates against petty pests, he demands proof of real fieldcraft: the tracking and clean harvest of one of Mulgore's most renowned wandering beasts.

The quarry is Arra'chea, a massive, legendary kodo whose looping trek winds across the golden grasses northeast of Thunder Bluff. To fell such a creature takes more than brute force; it demands patient stalking across the open savannah and respect for a titan of the plains. Bringing Arra'chea's horn back to the high rise earns not just personal glory, but provisions for the city, as Cairne immediately dispatches skinners and gatherers to ensure nothing of the sacred beast goes to waste.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: You have passed the Rites of the Earthmother and earned your place in Thunder Bluff.
But in order to maintain the spot that you strived so hard to achieve, you must continue to prove your worth to your people.
We are hunters, friend. Down below in Mulgore there is a mighty kodo named Arra'chea. Show me your skills in the ways of tracking and hunting by bringing me the Horn of Arra'chea.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Have you tracked down Arra'chea yet?

clips.title: Completion
paras: Well done! A fine kill that was.
I will send a gathering party to collect the carcass so we can retrieve the hide and meat.
You have done a great deed for your people, friend.
